title: Firehall Grocery Planning
subtitle: Lists that match crew size — not random cart chaos
description: Firehall grocery planning for station dinners: quantity lists, staple pantry, and shopping once for the week instead of three emergency runs.
intro: Grocery planning for the hall is half the battle. A list tied to one meal beats a cart full of 'maybe.' Start with crew count, pick a format (batch, line, grill), then buy protein first and starch second — everything else supports those two.

sections.heading: Build the list from the meal
paragraphs: Chili: meat, beans, tomatoes, onions, spices. Taco bar: protein, tortillas, toppings. Sheet pan: protein, peppers, oil, seasoning.

sections.heading: Pantry staples to keep stocked
paragraphs: Oil, salt, pepper, garlic, onions, rice, pasta, canned tomatoes, and foil. When these exist, dinner is a decision — not a store run.

practicalAdvice: Shop protein and starch first — veg and extras follow.
Buy one extra pound of protein — surprise visitors are normal.
Keep a laminated pantry list on the fridge.
Photo the receipt before you leave the store.

faqs.question: Where do these recipes come from?
faqs.answer: Each link goes to a full recipe on Firehall Meals — crew-sized portions, station timing, and steps written for a shared kitchen. Not home-blog scaling.

faqs.question: What if crew size or time changes tonight?
faqs.answer: Use Find a Meal with your headcount and minutes available. It pulls from the same hall-tested dinners these guides recommend.
